how: The surface view of Neptune made by functions (deep.ts). Lengths are in units of the close scene: the planet's radius is close.json radius, the camera of the approved close image stands 1 unit over the deck. u runs along the band (the great circle through closeup.json band), v across it, both from the point under that camera's nadir line; heights are over the smooth deck. Times are seconds from the middle of the surface view. Nothing here is a picture: every value below feeds a function of place, height and time. on: true draws this scene in the surface view and, by the eye's height, on the globe in the dive and the rise (globe below), so the film never shows two different places.

globe.how: The same scene on the globe in the dive and the rise; nothing here reads the clock. height: the eye's height over the planet in radii at which the scene first shows and at which it is drawn whole; between them it comes in over the globe's own map by the logarithm of the height. border: degrees from the place on the ground between which the scene ends and the globe's own map goes on (the horizon is 14 degrees away at 0.03 radii, so the surface view's field lies inside). fall: one grade for the globe and the scene by the eye's height, the way from the azure planet of the hold to the navy deck of the approved close image. Measured on globe alone against scene alone at 4715 to 4730 (assets-src/neptune/NOTES.md, 24 Nov 00:12): the pale band has one colour on both (pivot, linear light), the dark of the scene is the globe's to a power. Under the pivot a channel is drawn as pivot times (colour over pivot) to an exponent, over it unchanged: on the globe the exponent goes from 1 at the first height to power at the second, on the scene from 1 over power to 1, by the logarithm of the height. At the hold (2.07 radii) the globe is untouched, under the second height the scene is. blue: the most blue a graded colour of the globe keeps, as a multiple of its green, at the second height (over it the limit is this over the share of the grade, so there is none at the first height): the powers draw a deep blue of the map out to cobalt (seen at 4716 to 4720), the scene's own deck stands at 2.7. grid: a tool, 1 draws the scene's own coordinates on the deck, 2 and 3 write u and v of the deck under each pixel into the layers view (two bytes over 48 units, for measures); 0 in the film.

fan.how: What the eye of the surface view sees of the deck over its 180 frames (4770 to 4949), measured from the plan's poses (assets-src/neptune/NOTES.md, 24 Nov 01:55): a wedge on the ground. left, right: a point on each edge (u, v) and the bearing it runs at from the eye, in degrees from the u axis toward v; margin: how far the edges stand outside the measured footprint; far: the bearing of the middle line and how far along it the fan ends (the horizon of the eye is 9.2 units away, cirrus over it shows to 14); border: the distance outside the fan over which the scene of the approved close image gives way to the layout of the globe's own map. Inside the fan the scene is what the approved close image shows (the veil below; the streamers with where: map end at its border); outside it the scene is fitted to the map. veil: the pale far deck and the bright limb of the approved image are a thin sheet of ice haze over the deck, not a paler deck: seen from above it is nearly clear (depth: its optical depth straight down where it is thickest), along the low line of sight of the surface view the path through it is many times as long, so the far deck goes pale from the middle distance on and the limb bright, while the globe's own map under it (the dark oval) keeps its form from above. height: its underside and top; layers: how many layers the path through it is summed over; fall: the power by which it thins from its underside to its top (0: even), so the limb has no hard upper edge; light: what it scatters of the Sun toward the eye (times light.sun and the cirrus's lobe toward the Sun); shade: the share of its depth toward the Sun that it takes from the deck's light. It sets in between from and to of v + tilt times u (measured on the approved image), not west of west (u from, u to), and lies in bands along the flow of width wave across it and long times as long, with contrast; sizes: how many sizes of such bands lie over each other, each 0.41 of the one before; share: how much of it the thin bands lack. The eye never comes under it (the lowest eye of the film stands 0.97 over the deck).

steps.how: deck: steps of the relief march; shade: steps toward the Sun over the deck's own relief; cirrus: the most steps through the cirrus, each cirrusShare of its distance from the eye long; cirrusLimit: the shortest wavelength the cirrus keeps, in steps; light: taps toward the Sun inside the cirrus, the first lightStep long and each lightGrow times the one before, reading no wavelength shorter than lightLimit of the tap; cast: taps through the cirrus shell from the deck toward the Sun. cirrusSkip: where a step of the march finds the bent place outside every body, the march, the taps toward the Sun and the taps of the shadow go on by this share of its distance from the nearest body before they read again (0: every step is read). cirrusOpaque: the march ends where less than this share of what lies behind still comes through the cirrus. lightDeep: the optical depth toward the Sun past which the taps stop, since no light of the Sun comes through that the picture could show.

storm.how: at: u, v of the middle. eye: radius of the bowl. wall: shares of the eye radius between which the wall falls. depth: of the floor under the deck. reach: radius inside which the streaks wind round the storm. arms: count, pitch (turn per e-fold of radius; of the deck's octaves round the storm the longest take it whole and those as long as broad take none, deck lump), height, core (added to the radius under the logarithm), warp, light (how far an arm lifts the brightness), from (the shares of the eye radius between which the arms set in: under 1 they wind into the eye, so the eye is a whirl with a floor and no dark disc with a rim drawn round it). ragged: how far the deck's structure moves the wall in and out. spin: degrees a second at the middle, radius of half speed, share of it the arm pattern turns at. rings: the share of the deck's contrast the winding streaks keep at the storm's middle (they are fine rings, not a whirl). dark: the share of its brightness the deck loses on the floor of the eye. collar: the paler ring round the eye that the approved close image has: the radius from and to over which it ends, how far it lifts the brightness, and the share of it that follows the thin streaks, so the rim is made of streaks that fade outward and not of a disc with an edge.

wind.how: deck: speed along the band, jet (its swing across the band), jetWidth (units per radian of the swing), phase. cirrus: speed along the band and its shear across (per unit). row: the size of the rows (and rings) an octave rides in, in its own wavelengths.

deck.how: wave: the longest wavelength of the deck's structure. stretch: how far the longest octave is drawn out along the wind (share of its length across). lump: the power of the wavelength by which a shorter octave is drawn out less, until it is as long as broad (0: all octaves alike, streaks at every size), so the long waves are bands and the short ones cloud; the octaves round the storm follow the same rule from spiral.along up to spiral.across. curl: how far an octave is carried across the wind by each longer one, in wavelengths of that longer one (0: straight streaks). gain: weight of each octave against the one before. relief: height of the rolls. march: the shortest wavelength the relief march follows (finer relief shades by its slope only). life: how fast an octave of wavelength 1 changes of itself (per second, grows as the wavelength falls). colours are linear light before the film's exposure and tone curve: night (lowest), blue (middle), pale (highest). contrast: how far the structure moves the brightness. band: the lift of the pale deck outside the dark oval (vortex), then v from, v to over which it ends; near: v from, v to and the drop of the dark near deck, then v from, v to over which it begins (both ends lie past the horizon of the surface view). bounds: the highest and the lowest the deck can stand, for the march. west: u from, u to and the drop of the deck inside the fan west of the storm, where the approved close image is dark. level: the brightness without structure.

vortex.how: The wide dark zone the place lies in: the dark oval of the globe's own map, measured from above in these coordinates (assets-src/neptune/NOTES.md, 24 Nov 00:58). at: its middle (u, v); semi: its half length along the band and half width across; rim: the distance from the middle, in shares of the oval, between which the pale deck outside it sets in; warp: how far the deck's structure moves that rim; south: v from, v to over which the pale deck outside begins (south of the oval the map is not pale).

wisp.how: The thin bright streaks: the ridges of the octaves from number from on, each raised to power, each weighing gain of the one before; light: how far they lift the brightness; mean: what is taken off so the deck keeps its level; where: the range of the structure over which they come in. limit (above): the shortest wavelength drawn, in footprints of a pixel on the deck. near: the share of the streaks the dark near deck keeps. far: v from, v to over which the streaks of the far field grow, and how much more they lift the brightness there (the approved close image has long fine streaks along the limb).

cirrus.how: shell: lowest and highest height any cirrus can stand at. streamers (the first three are those of the approved close image; the fourth is the bright bow west of the storm and the fifth the band of cirrus on the far rim of the dark oval, both where the globe's own map has them from above): line (u from, u to, v at from, v at to), bow (how far its middle stands across the straight line, so it runs as an arc), wide (the width at the two ends as shares of halfWidth), halfWidth, base (height of its underside), thick, density, ends (length over which it fades at each end), lump (length of its thick and thin parts), lumpShare, seed, bend (the share of the bend of the line, warp below, that this streamer takes: 1 whole, less for a thin far one that stays a line), where (all: everywhere; map: a streamer of the globe's own map that the approved close image does not have, it ends at the border of the fan). lee: how much wider the side away from the Sun trails; leeSun: the same for the side toward the Sun (1: as wide as the crest). wave, stretch, rise, gain, octaves: the noise that tears it (rise: how far it is drawn out upward against across). erode: how much of the body the noise eats; soft: the density range over which it sets in. sigma: extinction per unit of density and length. A streamer is a chain of heaps with fibres blown off it (assets-src/neptune/NOTES.md, 24 Nov 02:57 to 03:11). The heaps: the narrow crest of the body, eaten by the noise, the density by the square so the edges are soft; core: the share of that eating the middle of the crest is spared. The fibres: the whole body with its trail on both sides, of density leeThin against the heaps, eaten 1 plus leeErode times as much; fringe: the density range over which the fibres set in, the share of the trail the side toward the Sun has, and the heights (shares of the thickness) between which the fibres end upward. billow: how far the first octaves are drawn out along the wind (near 1: round heaps) and how many they are; the finer ones are drawn out to stretch where the trail is. sweepDeg: the angle the grain of the noise stands at to the wind. warp, warpWave, warpNext: how far and at what wavelength the line of a streamer is bent, and size and reach of each next bend against the one before. floor: what is taken off the body so that it ends. castWave: the shortest wavelength of the noise that the shadow on the deck reads; cast: how many times its own depth toward the Sun the cirrus takes from the deck's light (the fibres finer than castWave are not in the shadow's taps). life: how fast an octave changes of itself.

haze.how: Two layers of air whose density falls with height: low (the bright line at the limb and the pale far deck) and high (the wide blue glow). depth: optical depth straight down from space; scale: the height over which it falls by e; colour: what it scatters of white sunlight. forward: weight and sharpness of the lobe toward the Sun. top: height where the drawn shell ends.

light.how: sun: the strength of the far Sun (linear light before exposure). sky: what the deck gets from above without the Sun. cloud: what the cirrus gets from the deck below and from the air. forward: weight and sharpness of the cirrus's lobe toward the Sun. wrap: how far the deck's light wraps past the edge of the Sun's reach. through: what the cirrus lets down to the deck beside the straight beam, light scattered on through the cloud: its share and how fast it dies with the cloud's depth, so the shadow of a streamer is dark and not black. cirrus: the share of the Sun the cirrus sends on. deep: light that reaches the inside of a cloud by scattering, twice a share and how fast it dies with the depth toward the Sun. shadow: how soft the shade of the deck's own relief is.
